steps.title: 2017: China, America's largest supplier
text: In 2017 the United States imported **$505 billion** of goods from the Chinese mainland, **21.6%** of all its imports and more than from the whole EU ($435 billion).
The map shows where US imports came from.

steps.title: 2018: tariffs and retaliation
text: From **6 July 2018** the US charged an extra 25% on $34 billion of Chinese imports, and later extended tariffs to more goods. China answered with tariffs on US goods, including 25% on soybeans.
US imports from China fell from $538 billion in 2018 to **$449 billion** in 2019 (−17%). The map shows the change from 2018.

steps.title: Soybeans go to Brazil
text: China imports more soybeans than any other economy. US soybean exports to China fell from **$13.9 billion** in 2016 to $7.1 billion in 2018, while China's soybean imports from Brazil rose from $14.5 billion to **$27.0 billion**.
Each line is one of China's soybean suppliers (CEPII BACI).

steps.title: Supply chains move
text: US buyers turned to other suppliers. From 2017 to 2024 imports from Mexico rose **62%** to $506 billion, and from Vietnam nearly tripled to $137 billion. In 2023 Mexico overtook the Chinese mainland as the largest single-country source of US imports.
China's share of US imports fell from 21.6% in 2017 to **13.4%** in 2024. Click a line to compare it with the US in the panel.
